interest: Shows 1947 War-State friction over Japan's reparations survey, with the Strike mission and FEC policy pulling in opposite directions.
overview: This file (July 22 – August 21, 1947) covers high-level U.S. interdepartmental negotiations and multilateral Far Eastern Commission (FEC) actions concerning Japanese reparations, level-of-industry standards, and the reduction of Japan's industrial war potential. The early portion contains an exchange between Assistant Secretary of War Howard C. Petersen and Assistant Secretary of State John H. Hilldring resolving differences over the War Department's contract with Overseas Consultants, Inc. (headed by Clifford S. Strike) to perform an independent engineering survey and audit of Japanese industrial plants without contravening approved U.S. policies like SWNCC 236/43 or Allied commitments. The latter portion consists of Far Eastern Commission Policy Decision FEC-084/19 (unanimously adopted August 14, 1947) defining rules for the destruction, reparations removal, and permissible retention levels of Japanese primary and war-supporting industries, accompanied by an interpretive statement by China and a State Department transmittal memorandum routing the resulting draft directive through SWNCC and the Joint Chiefs of Staff to General Douglas MacArthur (SCAP).

subfiles.about: Clarifies the War Department's rationale for hiring Overseas Consultants, Inc. to audit plant selections for Japanese reparations and addresses State Department concerns regarding unilateral action.
subfiles.from: Howard C. Petersen, Assistant Secretary of War
subfiles.summary: Petersen tells Hilldring an independent Strike-led audit of Japan's reparations plants was requested by MacArthur, warns of possible unilateral US action if the FEC stalls, and asks for an urgent conference.
subfiles.title: Letter from Howard C. Petersen to John H. Hilldring on Overseas Consultants Contract and Industrial Survey
subfiles.to: John H. Hilldring, Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Announces the War Department's engagement of Overseas Consultants, Inc. to evaluate Japan's industrial potential and assets available for reparations removals.
subfiles.summary: War Department announces Clifford Strike's eleven-firm consortium will survey Japanese industry for reparations, at MacArthur's request.
subfiles.title: War Department Press Release on Overseas Consultants Survey of Japanese Industry

subfiles.about: Expresses satisfaction that differences between the State and War Departments regarding the Overseas Consultants mission have been resolved.
subfiles.from: John H. Hilldring, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Hilldring welcomes resolved differences over the Strike mission, asking its reports be shared regularly with State.
subfiles.title: Letter from John H. Hilldring to Howard C. Petersen Resolving Differences over Strike Mission
subfiles.to: Howard C. Petersen, Assistant Secretary of War

subfiles.about: Sets forth specific instructions to be issued to Overseas Consultants, Inc. regarding adherence to SWNCC 236/43 and approved policy decisions.
subfiles.from: Howard C. Petersen, Assistant Secretary of War
subfiles.summary: Petersen clarifies Overseas Consultants won't challenge Japan's set industry level, only flag errors found.
subfiles.title: Letter from Howard C. Petersen to John H. Hilldring Defining Operational Instructions for Overseas Consultants
subfiles.to: John H. Hilldring, Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Transmits the Far Eastern Commission's unanimously adopted policy decision on Japanese industrial war potential reduction and a Chinese statement for implementation by SCAP.
subfiles.from: Samuel S. Stratton, Acting Secretary General, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.summary: Stratton transmits the FEC's August 1947 policy on reducing Japan's industrial war potential, asking State prepare directives for MacArthur and include China's interpretive statement.
subfiles.title: Letter from Samuel S. Stratton to Robert A. Lovett Transmitting FEC Policy Decision on Reduction of Japanese Industrial War Potential
subfiles.to: Robert A. Lovett, Acting Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Establishes Allied policy governing the destruction, reparations removal, and capacity limitations of Japan's war and war-supporting industries.
subfiles.summary: This comprehensive policy decision sets forth detailed measures to eliminate Japan's war-making potential during the occupation. It mandates the destruction of all specialized combat-equipment machinery and provides that primary war facilities, as well as excess capacity in designated war-supporting industries (including steel, chemicals, shipbuilding, and machine tools), be made available for reparations. Permissible productive capacity ceilings are established until October 1, 1949, or the conclusion of the current occupation phase, subject to subsequent FEC review and peace treaty terms. The Supreme Commander is authorized to grant temporary retention exceptions for occupation necessities after consulting the Allied Council for Japan and is instructed to maintain complete records of all removals and destruction.
subfiles.title: Far Eastern Commission Policy Decision FEC-084/19: Reduction of Japanese Industrial War Potential
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (via U.S. Government)

subfiles.about: Records the official statement of the Chinese representative regarding the interpretation and implementation of FEC-084/19.
subfiles.from: Chinese Delegation to the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.summary: China's FEC statement limits reparations delays' effect on claimant shares, and clarifies which heavy-machinery types count.
subfiles.title: Excerpt from FEC Draft Minutes: Chinese Statement on Reduction of Japanese Industrial War Potential

subfiles.about: Transmits the draft directive based on FEC-084/19 to SWNCC for forwarding through the Joint Chiefs of Staff to General MacArthur.
subfiles.from: Charles E. Saltzman, Special Assistant to the Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Saltzman forwards the FEC's industrial-reduction directive to SWNCC for transmission to MacArthur via the Joint Chiefs.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Charles E. Saltzman to SWNCC Transmitting Draft Directive on Reduction of Japanese Industrial War Potential
